note: Change a level here (A1–C2); the daily tasks read it before writing. English, German, French and Spanish come Monday to Friday; the weekend is for review. French: ONE article a day, level rotating by weekday (levels.fr). Spanish (Latin American) for a friend: two items Monday to Friday, levels by weekday in levels.es.

themes.Thu: Ungerade ISO-Wochen: Bücher & Lesen; gerade: Natur & Wissen

topics: world curiosities — especially East Asia, South Asia, Africa, Latin America

schedule.en: PAUSED since 2026-11-03 (the owner has plenty to read); the earlier English articles stay as a library.
schedule.de: PAUSED since 2026-11-03 (the owner has plenty to read); the earlier German articles stay as a library.
schedule.fr: Mon–Fri: 1 article, level by weekday (A1, A2, B1, B2, C1)
schedule.pt: Every day three A1 items: diary + dialogue + Textinho. Saturday: the A1 song story replaces the dialogue (diary + song story + Textinho). Extras for the heritage-speaker friend at B1/B2 (not counted, invisible at A1): Wednesday crônica, Saturday B1/B2 song story.
schedule.picks: PAUSED since 2026-11-03 together with English and German.
schedule.weekend: Saturday and Sunday: no new English, German or French texts (no weekly review).
schedule.es: Mon–Fri around 18:00: 2 items, Latin American Spanish (ustedes, no vosotros) — one reading (culture, feminism, everyday life) and one conversation dialogue (small talk, asking questions, directions), levels rotating A1–B2 by weekday, with a short grammar note. Helper languages: English and German.
schedule.limit: EN/DE/ES: two items Mon–Fri; FR: one item Mon–Fri; PT: three A1 items every day; picks lists don't count.
schedule.records: Once a month (1st): +2 records each for pt and es, and a new card batch for Coisas do Brasil and Cosas de Latinoamérica.
schedule.wordbank: Tuesday and Friday nights: only Spanish (A2→B1→A1→B2) and German UG grow; pt/de/en/fr CEFR decks are paused (enough cards for now).

pt_focus.format: Three A1 items every evening: (1) Diário da Ana (first-person diary, full date, clock times, today's weekday focus); (2) a short everyday dialogue (8–12 lines) — on Saturday replaced by the A1 'Histórias de canções' item from the Saturday task; (3) a very short real-life text, "Textinho" (40–90 words). New glossary words of the day go into the flashcards (data/pt-BS.json).

topics_by_weekday.Mon: datas, horas e dias da semana + perguntas sobre estudos e profissão
topics_by_weekday.Tue: adjetivos e locuções adjetivas: concordância (o bolo gostoso, a casa amarela, os gatos pretos), posição depois do substantivo, substantivo + de + substantivo (bolo de chocolate, suco de laranja, casa de praia, comida de mãe) vs. de + artigo para posse (o bolo da mãe); + plural e masculino/feminino
topics_by_weekday.Wed: números (contando em português: idades, preços, telefones, horários)
topics_by_weekday.Sun: preposições (em, de, para, com, a, por + contrações no, na, do, da)

learned: dates, months, days of the week, time
Adjetivos e locuções adjetivas (substantivo + de + substantivo)

dialogue_focus.topic: perguntas: pronomes interrogativos (que / o que, quem, onde, de onde, aonde, quando, como, qual / quais, quanto / quanta / quantos / quantas, por que vs. porque, a que horas, com quem, para quem) + yes/no questions with rising intonation, "né?", "Tudo bem?"
dialogue_focus.note: Until this date the dialogue (and the Textinho, where natural) practises asking questions instead of the weekday topic; the diary keeps the weekday topic. After it, the dialogue follows topics_by_weekday again.

textinho_rotation.Tue: um bilhete ou recado (na geladeira, para a vizinha)
textinho_rotation.Wed: um cardápio, uma lista de preços ou um anúncio pequeno
textinho_rotation.Fri: uma placa ou um aviso (na padaria, no prédio, no metrô)
textinho_rotation.Sat: um cartão-postal ou uma mensagem de voz transcrita
textinho_rotation.Sun: uma agenda ou lista de tarefas da semana

es_focus.who: A friend at A2 who wants to talk to people; material A1–B2, most of it A2–B1.
readings_rotate: Latin American culture & customs (one country at a time: México, Colombia, Argentina, Chile, Perú, Cuba, Guatemala, Bolivia, Uruguay, Ecuador…)
feminism & women in Latin America (movements, writers, artists, everyday questions — factual, no invented quotes)
día a día: food, markets, buses, family, work, festivals, money, apartments, weather
dialogues_rotate: small talk (meeting people, plans, hobbies, weather, compliments)
asking questions (in a shop, at a café, at the doctor's, at a hostel, on the phone)
directions (on foot, by bus/metro, asking twice, understanding landmarks)
grammar_path: perífrasis: ir a, acabar de, estar + gerundio
es_focus.easter_eggs: each item may end with a small 'dato curioso' or a regional word (e.g. México vs Argentina vs Colombia) — true facts only.

helper_languages.rule: Write only these fields. Missing fields are fine: the app falls back to English, then Chinese.

de.glossary: {w, de, zh} — de = simple German explanation (main)

fr.glossary: {w, fr, de} — fr = simple French explanation (main)

helper_languages.tags: every new item gets "tags": 2–4 short strings (country/region, topic or situation, grammar point), read by tools/mg_recent.py
